title: MCP add silently ignores unknown fields and its reminder names the CLI flag
outcome: MCP add silently ignores unknown fields and its reminder names the CLI flag
acceptance: An MCP word call with an unknown argument (for example `accept` on add) is refused naming the unknown field and the accepted ones, instead of being dropped silently
Tests cover both; the full quality gates pass
The defaulted-acceptance reminder on MCP names the MCP field (`acceptance`), not the CLI flag `--accept`

completion.summary: All 15 MCP argument structs deny unknown fields. A call with an unlisted argument, such as accept on add, is refused before any read or write, with rmcp relaying serde's "unknown field `accept`, expected one of … `acceptance` …", and each input schema carries additionalProperties: false. The defaulted-acceptance reminder names the MCP field ("set acceptance") on MCP, through a private ArgumentNames setting that McpServer selects, and keeps "set --accept" on the CLI. Covered by an mcp.rs unit test and a dogfood test across all 15 tools. Landed as a1e959f; installed as build a4c0b90d94ef; TermAl notified. Other MCP guidance strings that still name CLI flags are filed as w-5a66f5ebc5cd.
